notes.heading: Track the subject through questions and connected clauses
paragraphs: Spanish verb endings often identify the subject even when a pronoun is omitted. A reply changes perspective: a question about tú may require a yo answer. Coordinated subjects containing yo normally correspond to nosotros or nosotras, and the ending must change accordingly. Place no directly before the conjugated verb for these simple negative statements. Regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs share some endings but differ in others, especially the nosotros form. Accent marks are part of the written form and should be retained when required.

questions.prompt: Answer '¿Vives en Quito?' by saying that you live in Lima and do not live in Quito, using complete regular present-tense clauses.
questions.answer: Vivo en Lima y no vivo en Quito.
solution: The reply describes the speaker, so use the yo form vivo.
Place no before the second conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: Complete with regular present-tense nosotros forms: 'Nosotros ___ español, ___ fruta y ___ en Madrid.' Use estudiar, comer and vivir.
questions.answer: Nosotros estudiamos español, comemos fruta y vivimos en Madrid.
solution: Use -amos for estudiar, -emos for comer and -imos for vivir.
Keep the plural first-person subject across all three clauses.

questions.prompt: Correct 'Ana y yo no trabaja los sábados' and explain both the subject interpretation and negative placement.
questions.answer: Ana y yo no trabajamos los sábados.
solution: Ana y yo corresponds to nosotros or nosotras.
Use trabajamos; no is already correctly placed before the verb.
markingPoints: Retain and explain no before the verb.
